JUSTICE
REKHA BORANA Order 09/07/2024 1.

The present writ petition has been preferred with the following prayers:-
"i) That by an appropriate writ, order and direction may kindly be issued and report and order dated 28.05.2024 (Annex.22), order dated 28.05.2024 (Annex.23), order dated 30.5.2024 (Annex.24), [2024:RJ-JD:29123] (3 of 9) [CW-11014/2024]
communication dated 10.6.2024 (Annex.25), dated 14.6.2024 (Annex.27) & dated 18.6.2024 (Annex. 28) passed by the Tehsildar Luni/SDO Luni and the District Collector Jodhpur may kindly be quashed and set adide and further the authority may directed to determine the compensation according to the provision of the Land Acquisition Act, 2013.

ii) That by an appropriate writ, order and direction may kindly be issued and the respondents may kindly be restrained to raise any transmission tower or line Laduram vs State Of Rajasthan (2024:Rj-Jd:29123) on 9 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/68302103/
2

from/over the land of the petitioner until the acquisition is not made under a valid notification or the process of law, the respondent may also directed for determine the compensation against the use of land under the provision of land acquisition Act,
2013.

iii) That by an appropriate writ, order and direction may kindly be issued and respondents may restrict to interference in the right of the petitioners over the land in question as mentioned in Annexure-3 of the writ petition.

iv) That by an appropriate writ, order and direction may kindly be issued and the respondents may kindly be prohibited to construct the transmission tower/line upon the land of petitioners without passing any order/award of the compensation by the competent authority for use of the land.
v) Any other appropriate order or direction which this Hon'ble Court may deem fit just and proper in the facts and circumstances of the case may kindly be passed in favour of the petitioner.
vi) Costs of the writ petition may kindly be awarded to the petitioner."

2. The facts of the case are that two writ petitions were preferred by the petitioners being SBCWP No.17859/2023 and [2024:RJ-JD:29123] (4 of 9) [CW-11014/2024] 19411/2023 with the submission that a project for "765 KV double circuit power transmission connecting Beawar and Fatehgarh-3"
has been undertaken by the respondent department and the respondent No. 4 Company has been chosen for implementing the said project.

It had been mentioned in the petitions that the transmission line passes directly through the land owned by the petitioners, yet no compensation has been determined for utilization of land of the petitioners.
3.

In the said writ petitions, a submission was made by learned counsels appearing on behalf of the State as well as the Company that the concerned authority shall determine the compensation to be paid to the petitioners and on such determination, the amount shall be paid to the petitioners.

On said submission been made by the respective counsels, the writ petitions were disposed of vide order dated 16.04.2024 with a direction to the Collector, Jodhpur/ Sub Divisional Officer, Luni to determine the compensation within a period of two weeks after affording reasonable opportunity of hearing to all the concerned parties.
The determination of the amount of compensation was directed to be made in accordance with the guidelines dated 15.10.2015 as issued by the Government.
It was further directed that the amount so determined be paid to the petitioners within a period of four weeks of the determination.
4. In pursuance to order dated 16.04.2024, notices were issued to the respective petitioners and in response, they preferred their claim petitions before the SDO.

The SDO, vide letter dated Laduram vs State Of Rajasthan (2024:Rj-Jd:29123) on 9 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/68302103/
3 28.05.2024, submitted to the Collector, the determination of compensation as made by him and requested for [2024:RJ-JD:29123] (5 of 9) [CW-11014/2024] appropriate directions for deposition of the compensation amount.
After appropriate directions, the amount as determined, was deposited by the company in the account of SDO, Luni on 12.06.2024.

5. The case of the petitioners in the present writ petition is that the alleged determination has not been made by the SDO in terms of the guidelines or in accordance with the provisions of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act,
2013 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act of 2013').
6.

entities.text:
Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act,
2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the petitioners submitted that the claim petition as preferred by the petitioners was not even decided by the SDO and hence, there was no determination in terms of law.

It has further been submitted that no survey, which ought to have been conducted by the Tehsildar,
had been conducted and therefore, the alleged determination is no determination in eyes of law.

7. Per contra, learned Senior counsel appearing on behalf of the respondent Company submitted that the present writ petition is a clear abuse of process of law as a Special Appeal (D.B. Civil Special Appeal (Writ) No.580/2024) against the order dated 16.04.2024 as passed by the learned Single Judge, had already been preferred by the petitioners.
In the said appeal, the grounds as raised before this Court have already been raised and the said appeal remains pending as on date.
The fact of an appeal having been filed, the interim order having been passed in the said appeal and the appeal being pending as of date, have malafidely been concealed in the present writ petition.

Learned Senior counsel further submits that the issue whether the compensation is to be determined in accordance with Act of 2013, being already subjudice before the Division Bench, the same can neither be permitted to be raised before this Court nor can this Court entertain the same.

9. He further submits that alternative remedy in terms of Section 67(4) of the Electricity Act, 2003 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act of 2003') as well as under Section 16 of the Indian Telegraph Act,
1885 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act of 1885') is available to the petitioners.
He submits that the determination of compensation, whatsoever, is amenable to challenge in terms of the above provisions and hence, the present writ petition cannot be entertained.

In support of the submission,
he relied upon the verdict passed in the case of Power Grid Corporation of India Ltd. Vs. Century textiles & Industries Ltd. & Ors; (2017) 5 SCC 143.
10.

entities.text: Power Grid Corporation of India Ltd. Vs. Century textiles & Industries Ltd. & Ors; (2017) 5 SCC 143
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Heard learned counsels and perused the record.

11. What is evident in the present matter is that a Special Appeal assailing the order dated 16.04.2024 has already been preferred by the petitioners wherein specific ground of compensation to be made in terms of the Act of 2013 has been raised.

In the said appeal, on 30.05.2024, Hon'ble Division Bench observed and ordered as under:-
Laduram vs State Of Rajasthan (2024:Rj-Jd:29123) on 9 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/68302103/
4
"Learned counsel for the petitioner fairly submits that issue is about compensation to be paid in lieu of the direction of the tower and the right of way.

Learned counsel further submits that compensation has to be granted in [2024:RJ-JD:29123] (7 of 9)
[CW-11014/2024] accordance with Schedule IV of the Act of 2013.

Learned Sr. Counsel Mr. MS Singhvi submits that they shall abide by the judgment laid down by the learned Single Judge of this Court at this juncture and rest of the things can remain final outcome of the appeal.

Due to paucity of time, there is second last working day of the summer vacation, learned AAG is directed to take necessary steps for the compliance of the impugned order subject to the final out come of the appeal.
List this matter on 04.07.2024."

12. Further on 04.07.2024, Hon'ble Division Bench observed and ordered as under:-
"Learned counsel for the appellants prays that he may be granted short adjournment to argue the matter.
Learned Senior Counsel appearing for the respondents submits that though there is no interim order, the appellants are obstructing installation of tower.

It is made clear that this Court has not passed any interim order in the case and the order passed by the learned Single Judge entitles the appellants to receive compensation, which has already been deposited by the respondents as per the direction of the Court and the appellants may collect the same from the office of Sub-Divisional Officer.
The respondents will be free to proceed with their work.
List this matter after two weeks."

13. A bare perusal of the order dated 30.05.2024 as passed by the Hon'ble Division Bench makes it clear that the ground of [2024:RJ-JD:29123] (8 of 9) [CW-11014/2024] determination of compensation to be made in accordance with Schedule IV of the Act of 2013 had also been raised and the Hon'ble Division Bench had specifically observed that the said ground shall remain subject to the final outcome of the appeal.

Further, vide order dated 04.07.2024, the respondents were directed to proceed with the work and the appellants therein were given liberty to collect compensation deposited by the company from the office of the Sub-Divisional Officer.

14. In view of the above facts, this Court is of the clear opinion that after the orders dated 30.05.2024 and 04.07.2024 having been passed by the Hon'ble Division Bench, the writ petition on the same grounds could not have been preferred by the present petitioners.

The present writ petition had been preferred on 04.07.2024 and as is evident, the Special Appeal had been preferred prior to Laduram vs State Of Rajasthan (2024:Rj-Jd:29123) on 9 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/68302103/
5 the said date.
The fact of the Special Appeal having been filed and the order dated 30.05.2024 having already been passed in the said appeal has clearly not been mentioned in the present writ petition.
In the specific opinion of this Court, the same clearly amounts to concealment of material facts.

15. So far as the grounds as raised by learned counsel for the petitioners that the SDO did not determine the compensation in terms of law and the Tehsildar did not make any survey as required are concerned, alternative remedy in terms of Section 67(4) of the Act of 2003 as well as in terms of Section 16 of the Act of 1885 is very well available to the petitioners.
The petitioners, if aggrieved of alleged determination of compensation, [2024:RJ-JD:29123] (9 of 9) [CW-11014/2024] could very well have availed the remedy as provided under the said Acts.
16. In view of the aforementioned alternative remedy as provided under the said Acts also, this Court is not inclined to entertain the present writ petition.
17. In view of the above overall analysis and in view of the evident concealment of material facts, as discussed above, the present writ petition is dismissed with a cost of Rs.10,000/-.
18. Stay petition also stands disposed of.
